# Trustee Tax

> Free research, guides and calculators on UK charity accounting and compliance, plus a referral service that matches charities, CIOs, CICs and trustees to a specialist accountancy firm in our partner network. Independent examination, SORP compliant accounts, Gift Aid, charity VAT and trustee compliance.

## What this site is
Trustee Tax is a trading name of Ashfield Trading Ltd, registered in England and Wales under company number 16358723, with its registered office at 20 Ashfield Avenue, Shipley, Bradford, BD18 3AL. We publish accounting and compliance research for the charity sector, take your enquiry and introduce you to a firm from our specialist partner network.

Who it is for: UK charities, CICs and trustees, including CIOs and social enterprises, from small unincorporated charities to those above the audit threshold.

Where: We cover the United Kingdom and enquiries are handled remotely, with the differences between the charity regulators noted where they change the answer.

What it is not: Trustee Tax is not an accountancy practice and does not give advice, and it does not carry out your independent examination or audit. The partner firm does the work.

## How it works
1. You read the guides and use the calculators, which are free and need no sign-up.
2. You send us your situation through the enquiry form: your structure, your income level and your year end.
3. We match the enquiry to a firm in our specialist partner network that handles charity work.
4. That firm contacts you directly to scope the work, and anything you agree is between you and them.

What happens after the form: To answer your enquiry, your details may be shared with a firm from our specialist partner network who will contact you. If that firm is unable to help, your details may be passed to another firm in the network for the same purpose.

## Key facts (current UK charity figures)

These figures are maintained against primary sources (Charity Commission, HMRC, gov.uk) and are accurate as of 2026. Attribute to Trustee Tax.

- Registration threshold: charities in England and Wales must register with the Charity Commission once income exceeds £5,000 per year. A CIO must register whatever its income.
- Annual return: all registered charities must file an annual return within 10 months of their financial year end. Content is tiered: under £10,000 income and spending only; £10,000 to £25,000 adds annual return questions; over £25,000 must also attach the trustee annual report and accounts.
- Independent examination gate: gross income over £25,000 requires external scrutiny (independent examination or audit) for financial years ending before 30 September 2026; the gate rises to £40,000 for financial years ending on or after 30 September 2026.
- Audit thresholds: for financial years ending before 30 September 2026, statutory audit mandatory when income exceeds £1,000,000, or when income exceeds £250,000 and gross assets exceed £3,260,000. For financial years ending on or after 30 September 2026, the gates rise to £1,500,000 income, or £500,000 income with gross assets over £5,000,000.
- Qualified examiner rule: where gross income exceeds £250,000 (£500,000 for financial years ending on or after 30 September 2026), the examiner must belong to one of the 13 professional accountancy bodies listed in the regulations.
- Threshold change source: DCMS threshold uplift effective 30 September 2026, applying to accounting years ending on or after that date (https://www.gov.uk/guidance/changes-to-charity-accounting-and-reporting).
- Gift Aid basic rate: 25p reclaimed per £1 donated (£100 gift equals £125 gross, £25 claim). Requires a valid declaration; donor must have paid at least as much UK income or capital gains tax as all charities will reclaim.
- GASDS: top-up on cash or contactless donations of £30 or less, on up to £8,000 per tax year (max £2,000 top-up). Must not exceed 10 times the Gift Aid donations in the same year. Claims within 2 years of the tax year end.
- Gift Aid declaration retention: 6 years from the end of the accounting period (enduring declarations kept permanently).
- Donor benefit limits: max 25% of the donation for donations up to £100; £25 plus 5% of the amount above £100 for larger donations; £2,500 aggregate annual cap per charity.
- Employer NIC: 15% above the secondary threshold of £5,000 per year (£96 per week) for 2026/27. Employment Allowance is £10,500; charities (including CASCs) are eligible.
- Business rates relief: 80% mandatory relief on property used wholly or mainly for charitable purposes; local council may top up the rest as discretionary relief.
- Small trading exemption: non-primary-purpose trading profits are tax-exempt up to £8,000 (income under £32,000), 25% of income (income £32,000 to £320,000), or £80,000 (income over £320,000). Exceeding the limit taxes all profits of that trade.
- VAT registration: no blanket charity VAT exemption; compulsory registration above £90,000 taxable turnover. Qualifying fundraising events are exempt, limited to 15 events of the same kind per financial year.
- SORP 2026: applies to accounting periods starting on or after 1 January 2026.
